subject: Nexus private deployment — safelist, firewall, and egress controls
messages:
From: Natalie Park <natalie@nhc-sec.com>
To: ava.chen@redwood.com
Cc: itops@nhc.nexus-health.com
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint egress requirements — Nexus Health question

Hi Ava,

We're preparing our VPC / on-prem network policy for the Redwood private deployment pilot and need to lock down the outbound (egress) controls and firewall allowlist. Security needs a tight, auditable statement of what IPs, ports, and domains will be used by Redwood control plane and model endpoints so we can produce a SOC-ready evidence package.

A few specific asks to get us moving:
- Canonical list of IP addresses and CIDR ranges we must allow for the control plane (TLS, telemetry, health checks).
- Any outbound port requirements (eg, 443 only? alternative TCP/UDP?).
- Whether Redwood supports routing via a customer-managed NAT/proxy (we prefer a single egress proxy for auditing).
- How ephemeral are the outbound addresses (static, ephemeral with rotation windows?), and whether you can provide an attestable rotation schedule.
- A short note on what metadata/certs are presented by control-plane endpoints (SNI, cert CN) so our TLS inspection rules can permit traffic.

We're on a tight approval timeline for this PoC—can you respond with a concise technical statement + an attachment we can hand to our auditors?

Thanks,
Natalie Park
Head of Security, Nexus Health

From: ava.chen@redwood.com <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Park <natalie@nhc-sec.com>
Cc: itops@nhc.nexus-health.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 12:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress requirements — Nexus Health question

Hi Natalie — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a one-page factsheet (redwood-egress-factsheet-v1.pdf) and a CSV safelist template to drop into your ticket system. High-level answers below; please flag anything you need formalized for auditors and we can add evidence (signed statement + control-plane cert chain).

Summary (short):
- Control plane: static / customer-bound IP ranges are available for Private deployments. For our hosted control plane we publish a stable set of egress IPs per region; for Private (VPC) we can either come through your NAT/proxy or, on Dedicated/Private, use a small set of reserved egress IPs we bind to the deployment.
- Ports: TLS 443 outbound is required for all control-plane telemetry, artifact pulls, and health pings. No UDP is required.
- Proxy/NAT: Supported. We recommend routing control-plane out via customer-managed NAT (preferred for auditability). We also support mTLS to the control plane if you require mutual auth.
- Ephemeral vs static: For Private deployments, egress IPs can be pinned (static) for the contract term. If you choose to use Redwood-managed egress, we offer weekly rotation windows with signed rotation manifests.
- SNI/certs: Control plane uses sni: control.redwood-inference.com and presents a public cert (CN=*.redwood-inference.com). We'll provide the full cert chain in the evidence bundle.

Requested next steps:
1) Tell us whether you will use your NAT/proxy (we'll provide the CSV template to populate).
2) If you need pinned IPs, confirm region and deployment size (small/standard/high) and we will reserve the minimum set.
3) Send any auditor-specific checklist items and we'll generate a signed attestation.

Attachment: redwood-egress-factsheet-v1.pdf (one-pager) and nexus-mrp-safelist-template.csv

Best,
Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: markus.klein@redwood.com <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: ava.chen@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 15:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress requirements — Nexus Health question

Thanks Ava — a couple of operational clarifications from infra: 

- If Nexus wants to terminate egress via their proxy, they must allow TLS passthrough for SNI inspection or we must provide the control-plane cert fingerprint ahead of time for outbound TLS termination. Full TLS interception will break mTLS unless we coordinate with their proxy vendor.
- For pinned IPs: we typically allocate 3 addresses for small, 5 for standard, 10 for high throughput. These are used for control plane + artifact pulls. If they plan model downloads (large weights) over the same channel, recommend separate bandwidth accounting and a larger allocation.
- If Nexus requires IP rotation auditing, we can emit signed rotation manifests weekly. Priyom, please add the rotation manifest template to the Drive link and note retention (90 days default).

Markus
Director, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference

From: Natalie Park <natalie@nhc-sec.com>
To: ava.chen@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: itops@nhc.nexus-health.com
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress requirements — Nexus Health question

Thanks Ava/Markus — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from our ops and audit teams: 

- Audit wants a signed statement that for the Private (VPC) deployment the egress IPs will remain static for at least 90 days and any rotation event will be pre-announced 7 days in advance (we can accept weekly rotation if pre-announced). Can Redwood provide that as an attested PDF?
- For the TLS interception note: our proxy vendor (SecureProxy) does break mTLS by default. We will need either TLS passthrough or an allowlist by cert fingerprint. Can you provide the cert fingerprint and the exact SNI string for the control plane?
- We prefer to route all control-plane egress via our NAT/proxy. Please confirm the CSV template fields and we will populate and return it in our ticket.

Also: can you attach any prior evidence packages (redacted) used for other healthcare customers? It helps accelerate our compliance review.

Natalie
